name: @silkweave/box-ui
description: The Box component library: design tokens, primitives and the app shell, free of tRPC, auth, the feature registry and the agent stack. Apps inject their data through the seams this package exports; a component without a story is not in the library.
//: No build. Both consumers (apps/web and Storybook) resolve the @silkweave/box-source condition to src/, and this package is private and never published - so a tsdown artifact would be untested by construction, and wrong: Wordmark's new URL('../assets/...', import.meta.url) has no assets/ under build/, and the stylesheets are not JS. `default` points at source too, so a consumer that does not set the condition still gets something that works.
//exports: Entry points are cut by DEPENDENCY FOOTPRINT, not taxonomy. '.' needs only React, base-ui, lucide and cva; anything heavier gets its own subpath and an OPTIONAL peer dependency (./board needs @dnd-kit, ./charts needs recharts, ./editor needs TipTap). This is forced by the no-build decision above: with src/ resolved directly, whatever '.' re-exports is walked by tsgo and Vite's scanner on every import, so re-exporting the editor would make a Box that never opens one fail to resolve TipTap. Tree-shaking never gets a say - resolution fails first.
//peerDependencies: The optional peers are the subpath entry points' dependencies: import @silkweave/box-ui/editor and you supply TipTap; import /board and you supply @dnd-kit; import /charts and you supply recharts. NOT `optionalDependencies`, which means 'install this but tolerate a failed build' and is installed for everyone. They are ALSO devDependencies so this package's own typecheck and Storybook can see them - harmless, since it is private and never published.
